clarity.justification: The proposal has a coherent directional mechanism and a generally aligned test: it contrasts activations before “genuine backtracks (that change the answer) versus reflexive ones,” then tests whether a detector signal “drives suppression of the just-generated path and elevation of alternative tokens.” However, key quantities such as “detector strength,” “useful backtracking,” and “efficiency” are not operationalized, and no numerical success or failure thresholds are given; the claim that the circuit is “largely absent in base models and emerges through RL training” therefore remains only partly decidable. The stimulation and suppression predictions are directionally falsifiable through “correction rate,” “accuracy gain,” and “loop reduction,” but an expert would still need clarification about the detector direction, event labels, comparison baselines, and what effect size would establish or refute the mechanism.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is identifying and causally interpreting the proposed “inconsistency detection heads” and then performing “inject detector-direction on error cases lacking backtracks”; activation hooks, head contrasts, path patching, and logit measurement are standard tooling, but the detector direction and its construction are custom and underspecified rather than fully runnable as written. The named Qwen base/distilled model family and activation-patching methods are supported by existing interpretability tooling, while the availability of the required matched “base model, an SFT checkpoint, and an RL checkpoint of the same family” and the stated “R1-Distill traces” is not established by the record; the limitation that “ideal base/RL pairs may be unavailable” is a substantive artifact-design risk, not merely an access issue. The proposal includes useful negative-result controls—“answer-changing vs non-changing,” “causal suppression on easy problems,” and “always-on/never”—but gives no sample sizes, model counts, dataset sizes, or other concrete resource figures, and the absence of explicit measurement protocols leaves feasibility at standard research complexity rather than near turnkey execution.
